title: Whiteboard write-up: the Keystone platform layer
scenario: Lumenfold is moving its sales, partner and renewals apps off a third-party CRM onto Keystone, a platform it builds and owns. You are in the first architecture session: turn the brief, the CRM inventory and the volumes into a platform design with service boundaries, a data model, interfaces (APIs, events, workflows, agent tools) and a migration path, plus two ADRs.
task: Requirements and non-goals, back-of-envelope scale from inputs/volumes.md
Service boundaries drawn around data ownership, with a diagram
Core data model for accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities and activities, multi-tenant
Interfaces: which capabilities are APIs, which are events, which are workflows, which are agent tools
Deep dives on the two riskiest parts, migration path off the CRM
ADR 0001 (tenancy model) and ADR 0002 (how services integrate)
acceptance: Graded by rubric only (grade.sh reports 0/0; the automated row does not apply)
Every table has exactly one owning service; no service reads another's tables
Numbers drive choices: storage, write rate, fan-out of the activity timeline
Each ADR has context, at least two real options, a decision and consequences

practices.label: Week 1 Tue - service boundaries, data ownership, multi-tenancy
Week 1 Wed - consistency, sagas and ADRs
Week 1 Thu - CRM domain: Salesforce objects, IDs, hidden logic
